breakpoints.note: The witness yields a full 0x200-byte header block whose first byte or prefix is non-zero and whose tar magic/checksum is accepted by `readRawHeader`, so `KTar::openArchive` stays in its header-processing loop instead of returning 0 or -1.

First project-code read on the vulnerable path: pulls 512 decompressed bytes from the attacker-controlled gzip/tar stream into `buffer` for tar-header parsing, and advances the logical archive position later reused by `seek`.

The fix replaces this single oversized read with a loop that limits each iteration to `qMin(bytesToRead, qint64(dummy.size()))`. In the vulnerable version there is no guard or chunking step tying the requested output length to `dummy.size()`.
